name: AlJazira Capital
legal_name: AlJazira Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company; one-person company owned by Aljazira Bank)
founded: 2008 (Ministerial Resolution S/57 dated 27 Feb 2008; CR 4030177603 dated 25 Mar 2008; operations began 5 Apr 2008 by taking over Bank AlJazira's brokerage division). CMA licence 07076-37 under CMA Resolution 2-38-2007 dated 22 Jul 2007. Head office moved from Jeddah to Riyadh in 2011 (CR 1010351313 dated 29 Sep 2012).
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by Aljazira Bank (100% at 30 Jun 2026 and 31 Dec 2025). Issued share capital SAR 500m (50m shares of SAR 10). The 2025 Board report of the bank shows it as a one-person company.
government_link: None identified. The parent bank has no government holder above 5% in its 2025 Board report (see sa-aljazira).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Aljazira Bank (sa-aljazira) and part of its 'Brokerage and asset management' segment. AlJazira Capital does not prepare consolidated statements: it is exempt as a subsidiary of Aljazira Bank (FY2025 FS accounting policies). It holds 3.72% of Aljazira Takaful (the bank holds 29.36% directly). Contracts and dealings with the bank were SAR 177m in 2025 (bank Board report). Double counting: AlJazira Capital's assets, income and AUM are consolidated in the bank's figures; never add this record's figures to sa-aljazira.
footprint: Saudi Arabia. Head office Riyadh (King Fahad Road, Al Rahmaniyah), with a branch in Jeddah (FS note 1). It moved to a new head-office building in 2025 (AR 2025). The executive bio of the Head of Wealth Management and Securities mentions sales centres in the Central and Western regions. Clients also reach it through Aljazira Bank. International brokerage covers selected GCC and international markets.
customer_segments: Individual investors (retail through HNW, including Aljazira Bank's affluent and private banking clients), institutions and HNW individuals (discretionary portfolios), family offices and sovereign and semi-government clients (asset management head's stated experience), corporates and issuers (investment banking), and financial institutions (custody and brokerage).
business_lines: Four lines per AR 2025: brokerage and securities; asset and wealth management; investment banking; own investments. FY2025 income (SAR '000, FS): asset and wealth management fees net 257,073; brokerage fees net 61,346; investment banking fees 21,225; custody fees 10,789; special commission income (mainly margin finance) 247,874; gain on financial instruments at FVTIS 78,880; dividend income 74,925; other 657; total 752,769. Services listed on the website: local, GCC and international brokerage, margin finance, sukuk, wealth management, public mutual funds, discretionary and non-discretionary portfolio management, Systematic Investment Plan, investment banking and services to financial institutions.

capabilities.wealth_summary: AlJazira Capital (CMA licence 07076-37; established 2008 from the bank's brokerage division) is Aljazira Bank's 100%-owned investment arm. In 2025 it reported total income of SAR 752.8m (+31.8%) and net income of SAR 342.2m (+49%), with AUM of SAR 28.4bn (+20%, first time above SAR 28bn) across 48 funds in private equity, private credit, real estate, operating leasing and money markets. Asset and wealth management fees rose 52% to SAR 257.1m while brokerage fees fell 34% to SAR 61.3m as Tadawul's average daily traded value dropped 30.6%. Clients trade and subscribe to funds through the 'Aljazira Tadawul' app and web platform, which uses TradingView analysis tools and offers a Systematic Investment Plan from SAR 100 a month. It offers discretionary and non-discretionary portfolio management and 'Intelligence-Led Wealth Management'. It launched a new brand identity and moved to a new head office in 2025. The 2026 plan is to grow asset and wealth management, hold brokerage share and keep developing digital services and alternative channels.

private_banking.detail: Private banking is run by the parent bank's Private Banking and Wealth Management Division (3 centres: Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar), which cooperates with AlJazira Capital for alternative-asset funds and other products (see sa-aljazira). AlJazira Capital's own wealth management service has no published eligibility or minimum.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 28.4bn at 31 Dec 2025 (SAR 23.7bn at 31 Dec 2024), 48 funds. Public mutual funds on the website fall into four categories: equity, money market, fund of funds (diversifying across several Shariah-compliant funds) and closed-ended real estate funds (small to medium residential projects). Private funds cover private equity, private credit, real estate and operating leasing. 2025 launches: Aljazira Evergreen Private Credit Fund and a health and nutrition private equity fund (Forbes ME). Four new real estate funds launched in H1 2026 (bank call). The Head of Real Estate has launched 20+ private real estate funds with assets above SAR 13bn. 2025 awards listed in the AR include Most Innovative Shariah-compliant Fund (Aljazira Open Fund), Most Innovative Real Estate Fund Manager in Saudi Arabia and best equity research house (The Global Economics and Finance International; which body gave which award is not clear from the extracted text).

brokerage.detail: Local (Tadawul Main Market and Nomu), GCC and international brokerage, plus sukuk trading and margin finance (margin finance receivables SAR 2.57bn at 31 Dec 2025). Channels: web platform, mobile app and a phone dealing centre. FY2025 brokerage fees SAR 61.3m (-34%). Website claims it is 'consistently one of the top-ranked executing broker' (self-reported). Own traded value and market share not disclosed. Research reports are published for the Saudi market.

digital_investing.detail: Official page 'Aljazira Capital APP and Platform': mobile app 'Aljazira Tadawul' (iOS and Android) and web platform (aljaziratadawul.com). Features: local stocks and sukuk plus selected GCC and international markets; subscribe to and redeem local and international funds including private funds; IPO participation; Systematic Investment Plan; consolidated portfolio with real-time profit tracking; research; technical and fundamental charts and economic calendar; margin lending; transfers between investment and bank accounts. The App Store listing (title 'Aljazira Capital'; seen in search results only) describes fund subscription, redemption and SIP. A separate App Store listing titled 'Aljazira Capital Global (GTN)' (search result only) suggests a GTN-built international trading app. The FAQ refers to a 'new AJC Platform and Application' without a date.

advisory.detail: CMA licence covers advising. The wealth management page offers 'Intelligence-Led Wealth Management' with specialists analysing global trends, a retirement planning focus and Shariah screening, with a 'Get in Touch with an Advisor' route. The site also lists CIO Office Insights and research reports.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary portfolio management for institutions and HNW individuals: clients authorise the Asset Management team under a discretionary agreement structured to risk appetite. Equity portfolios follow guidelines approved by the AlJazira Capital Sharia Board; a Murabaha variant is managed through the money market. No minimum, fee or reporting detail published. A non-discretionary management service is also listed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the website or app listing. The Systematic Investment Plan (standing instruction from SAR 100 or USD 30 a month into AlJazira Capital funds, matched to risk tolerance) is the nearest retail accumulation tool. 'CIO Office Insights' appears in the site navigation but was not opened.

funds_platform.detail: Distributes its own funds through the app, web platform, advisers and the parent bank. The fund-of-funds category invests across Shariah-compliant funds; whether these include third-party funds is not stated. No third-party fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the AlJazira Capital website pages checked (brokerage, asset management, wealth management) or in the AR 2025 text. The parent's Cayman subsidiary AlJazira Securities Limited handles Shariah-compliant derivatives for the bank, not clients.

private_markets.detail: Core growth area: 48 funds in private equity, private credit, real estate and operating leasing. Real estate: 20+ private funds above SAR 13bn (Head of Real Estate bio). 2025: Aljazira Evergreen Private Credit Fund and a health and nutrition PE fund targeting GCC growth companies. Private funds can be subscribed through the app (platform page).

islamic_wealth.detail: Funds and portfolios follow Shariah guidelines set by AlJazira Capital's Sharia committee (website and AR list a Shariah committee); Shariah-compliant equity, money-market and fund-of-funds funds, Murabaha discretionary variant, sukuk trading, SIP described as Shariah-compliant.

partners.what: Official app and platform page states 'Market analysis tools are provided by TradingView'

discrepancies.detail: The official page names the mobile app 'Aljazira Tadawul' (web platform aljaziratadawul.com). A search-result App Store listing is titled 'Aljazira Capital'. A second listing is titled 'Aljazira Capital Global (GTN)'.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the official name and the listing titles separately; whether these are one app or several was not confirmed (listing pages could not be opened).

discrepancies.detail: FS note 23 and the AR give SAR 28.4bn (AR also says 'exceeded SAR 28bn'). Forbes ME gives USD 7.6bn.

discrepancies.detail: Margin finance receivables (SAR 2.57bn) and clients' cash account (SAR 2.0bn) are separate from AUM.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded separately and not added to AUM.

discrepancies.detail: The Board report's attendance table is headed as covering meetings 'held during 2024' although the report is for 2025 and the four meeting dates (19 Mar, 25 Jun, 17 Jul, 14 Dec) match the 2025 committee reconstitution and board changes described in the same section.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as a typo; board membership and committee data were taken from the 2025 narrative (OGM 23 Jun 2025, term from 30 Jun 2025, CMA approval 3 Aug 2025). Minor.

Three further executives on the official page are not profiled (control functions): Ahmed Bin Nassar (Chief of Governance, Risk and Compliance Group; ex-Credit Suisse Saudi Arabia head of compliance), Fahad Al-Hudaib (Chief Human Capital Officer, joined 2012) and Sultan Alshalan (Chief Internal Audit).
